extName.description: The extension's name, in the store, toolbar and menus.

extDescription.message: Fill logins from the password vault on your Quark.
extDescription.description: The extension's description in the store and the extensions page.

commandFillLogin.message: Fill a login from Quark Vault
commandFillLogin.description: The keyboard shortcut's description on the browser's shortcuts page.

errorExtensionTooOld.message: This extension is too old for your Quark. Update the extension, then sign in again.

errorQuarkTooOld.message: Your Quark is too old for this extension. Update your Quark, then sign in again.

errorLegacyUpgrade.message: $HOST$ says this account was made before auth keys and needs your Quark password once to move it to one. After that, only the key is sent. Confirm below to send it this one time.

errorLegacyAgain.message: $HOST$ asked for your password again, but this account has already moved to an auth key, so the extension didn't send it. A Quark asks only once; this one may be misconfigured or not the server you think it is.

errorLegacyInsecure.message: $HOST$ asked for your password to move this account to an auth key, but the address uses plain http, so the extension didn't send it. Sign in once over https or in the Quark app, then try again.

errorSignedOut.message: Your Quark session ended. Sign in again.

errorAccountPending.message: This account is waiting for an admin to approve it.

errorNotAdmin.message: The vault needs an admin account.

errorLockedReason.description: REASON is the explanation the Quark gave, in English.

errorBadMasterPassword.message: That password didn't unlock the vault.

errorNotInitialized.message: The vault isn't set up yet. Create it in the Quark app first.

errorDriveDisconnected.message: The drive holding the vault is disconnected.

errorRateLimited.message: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.

errorNetwork.message: Couldn't reach your Quark. Check the address and that it's online.

errorServer.message: Your Quark couldn't finish that. Try again.

insecureServerRefusal.message: This Quark address uses plain http, so your passwords would cross the network unencrypted. Use an https address, or confirm that you understand the risk.

insecureServerWarning.message: Connected over plain http. Your passwords cross the network unencrypted. Switch to an https address.

refuseWrongSite.message: This login doesn't belong to this site.

refuseEmbeddedIn.message: This login form is embedded in $HOST$, so Quark Vault won't fill it.

refuseEmbeddedInPage.message: This login form is embedded in another page, so Quark Vault won't fill it.

refuseEmbeddedInSite.message: This login form is embedded in another site, so Quark Vault won't fill it.

refuseNoOtp.message: This login has no one-time code saved.

refuseNoFieldsReload.message: Couldn't find login fields on this page. If it just loaded, reload it and try again.

refuseNoFields.message: Couldn't find the login fields on this page.

refuseReload.message: This page can't be filled. Reload it and try again.

refuseTabMoved.message: This tab is now on $HOST$, not $CONFIRMED$. Open the popup again to fill it.

refuseSaveGone.message: That login is no longer waiting to be saved.

refuseNothingToUpdate.message: There's nothing to update for this login.

pageLocked.message: The vault is locked. Unlock it from the Quark Vault toolbar button.

menuNoLogins.message: No saved logins for this site

menuFillWhere.description: WHERE says where a login for another port or scheme was saved.

pickerSuggestHint.message: Fills this field and its confirmation

pickerFallbacks.message: Saved for another port or scheme

pickerNoLogins.message: No logins saved for this site

saveTitle.message: Save this login to Quark Vault?

updateTitle.message: Update the password in Quark Vault?

unlockToSaveTitle.message: Unlock Quark Vault to save this login

shortcutFirefoxChange.message: To change it, open about:addons, click the gear button, then Manage Extension Shortcuts.

shortcutFirefoxUnbound.message: Firefox didn't bind it. To set one, open about:addons, click the gear button, then Manage Extension Shortcuts.

shortcutUnbound.message: The browser didn't bind it, often because another extension has the same keys. Set one at $PAGE$.

welcomeNeedQuark.message: A Quark with the password vault set up, an admin account on it, and the vault password.

welcomeNeedAdmin.message: You sign in with the admin account first, then unlock with the vault password. Only admins can open the vault; if you aren't one, ask whoever runs your Quark.

welcomeNeedSessions.message: This browser shows up in your Quark's Settings › Sessions, where you can revoke it any time.

welcomeAddressFormat.message: Use https://your-quark when it has https, or http://host:port for a Quark on your own network, such as http://192.168.1.20:8080.

welcomeAddressInsecure.message: Plain http to another machine asks you to confirm first, because passwords would cross the network unencrypted.

welcomePermissionsTitle.message: Why it asks for these permissions

welcomeSitesFirefox.message: Access to your data for all websites: to find login forms on the pages you visit and fill them. Firefox asks for it separately; the popup shows Allow until you grant it.

welcomeSitesChrome.message: Read and change all your data on all websites: to find login forms on the pages you visit and fill them.

welcomePageSafety.message: A page never gets a password until you pick a login saved for that site, and your Quark session stays out of pages' reach.

welcomeOtherPermissions.message: Storage keeps your settings and sign-in, idle locks the vault when this computer locks, and the right-click menu offers Fill.

welcomeOptionalFirefox.message: Privacy and management, asked only if you choose to check for other password managers in the options.

welcomeOptionalChrome.message: Privacy and management (Manage your apps, extensions…), asked only if you choose to check for other password managers in the options.

addressCheck.message: Check the address, then try again.

addressTriedHttps.message: Tried $ORIGIN$. If your Quark serves plain http, edit the address to http://$HOST$.

addressTried.message: Tried $ORIGIN$. Check the address and port, and that your Quark is online.

builtInOn.message: The browser is still offering to save passwords.

builtInManaged.message: The browser's password saving is set by your organization or another extension.

builtInOff.message: The browser's password saving is off.

othersIntro.message: More than one manager filling the same form gets confusing. Turning one off keeps its saved passwords; you can turn it back on from $PAGE$.

othersBlocked.message: The browser didn't allow that change. Try it from $PAGE$ instead.

othersBuiltInHint.message: The browser can offer to save and fill passwords too.

othersExtensionsHint.message: Proton Pass, Bitwarden, 1Password and others. Checking asks for permission to manage extensions; Quark Vault only uses it to list password managers and to turn one off when you choose.

othersNone.message: No other password manager extensions are turned on.

optionsConnectHint.message: Open the Quark Vault toolbar button to connect.

optionsInlineButton.message: Show the Quark button in password fields

optionsInlineButtonHint.message: Only when the vault has an entry for the site

optionsBadge.message: Show the match count on the toolbar icon

optionsAutoSubmitHint.message: Off by default. Some sites need a second look first.

optionsLockingIntro.message: Locking from this browser locks the vault on your Quark for every device. The vault always locks when this computer's screen locks.

optionsLockOnIdle.message: Lock the vault when this computer is idle

optionsLockOnIdleHint.message: Off by default, so someone else mid-task isn't locked out

optionsIdleAfter.description: DURATION is a number of minutes, such as "15 minutes".

optionsShortcutHint.message: One match fills right away; several open the picker. Right-click a field for the same list. $STEPS$

optionsNeverSaveNone.message: None yet. Choose "Never for this site" when Quark Vault offers to save a login.

optionsServerAutoLock.message: The vault also auto-locks on the schedule set on your Quark.

popupConnectIntro.message: Sign in with an admin account; only admins can open the vault.

popupConnectIntroRevoke.message: Sign in with an admin account; only admins can open the vault. You can revoke this browser in Settings › Sessions.

popupInsecureAddress.message: This address uses plain http, not https. Your Quark password, vault password and every login you fill would cross the network unencrypted, where anyone on it can read them.

popupInsecureConfirm.message: I understand this connection is unencrypted

popupLegacyUpgradeConfirm.message: Send my Quark password to $HOST$ this one time

popupPersist.message: Stay signed in after the browser closes

popupWelcomeBanner.message: New here? What you need, and why.

popupWelcomeIntro.message: It fills logins from the password vault on your Quark.

popupLockedIntro.message: Unlocking here unlocks the vault on your Quark for every device, until it auto-locks.

popupCopiedCode.message: Copied the code for $NAME$. It changes in $SECONDS$.
popupCopiedCode.description: SECONDS is a short duration, such as "23s".

popupGenerated.message: Generated a password and copied it

popupSiteAccess.message: Allow Quark Vault on websites so it can fill logins there.

popupOthers.message: The browser or another password manager may also try to fill logins.

popupFillAnywaySavedFor.message: $NAME$ is saved for $SAVED$, not $PAGE$. Filling it here gives its username and password to $PAGE$.

popupFillAnywayNoSite.message: $NAME$ isn't saved for any site, not $PAGE$. Filling it here gives its username and password to $PAGE$.

popupFillAnywayHttp.message: $PAGE$ uses plain http, so they would also cross the network unencrypted.

popupFillAnywayTrust.message: Only fill it if you trust $PAGE$ with this login.

popupAutoLock.description: DURATION is a short number of minutes, such as "15 min".

popupEntriesHint.message: Entries are added in the Quark app, or when you save a login as you sign in.
